before.title: Framework-local SI units, the vacuum constants and the exact/measured status of their values
before.statement: Adopt the SI system of units for this framework, with the following quantity table and conventions; every symbol is a quantity of this framework and the laboratory structure is that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]. (a) [Coordinates and constants] $x^0=ct$ and each spatial coordinate $x^i$ carries the metre (m); the time coordinate $t$ carries the second (s); the conversion constant $c>0$ carries m s$^{-1}$ and has the exact SI defining value $c=299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the elementary charge $e$ has the exact SI defining value $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, and this item does not assert that physical charge is quantised; the magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ carries N A$^{-2}$ and is measured, so no exact numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted (at the adoption of the present SI definition of the ampere, $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}$ H m$^{-1}$ with relative standard uncertainty $2.3\times10^{-10}$); the electric constant is defined within the framework by $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in F m$^{-1}$, consistent with the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$, so that $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ and $\varepsilon_0$ inherits the relative standard uncertainty of $\mu_0$. (b) [Electromagnetic quantities] Charge $q$ carries the coulomb (C); the charge density $\rho$ of [[def-em-sources]] carries C m$^{-3}$ and the current density $J$ carries A m$^{-2}$, so that the four-current components $(c\rho,J)$ carry A m$^{-2}$; the electric field $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$; the magnetic field $B$ carries the tesla (T), where $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$; the scalar potential $\varphi$ carries V and the vector potential $A$ carries T m, so that the four-potential components $(\varphi/c,A)$ carry T m; the components of the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] carry T; a force carries the newton (N), $1\ \mathrm{N}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}$. (c) [Mechanical quantities] A rest mass parameter $m$ carries the kilogram (kg) and a four-momentum $P=mU$ carries kg m s$^{-1}$ ([[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]); field energy density carries J m$^{-3}$, energy flux W m$^{-2}$, so that $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}$. (d) [Bookkeeping only] The unit of a quantity records the adopted system of units; it does not show that a quantity is primitive in this or any other framework, it contains no measurement, and it does not identify a quantity with a similarly named quantity of another framework. The exact defining values of $c$ and $e$ fix numerical conventions of the SI, they do not by themselves identify $c$ with the vacuum propagation constant of ideal light, which is the physical adoption of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]].
before.strategy: A convention definition: it fixes the coordinate normalisation $x^0=ct$, the unit of each quantity used in this framework, the exact SI defining values of $c$ and $e$ and the measured status of $\mu_0$. The exact values $c=299\,792\,458$ m/s and $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and the statements that the new definition of the ampere fixes $e$ rather than $\mu_0$, that $\mu_0$ must now be determined experimentally, and that $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$ remains exact, are taken from the SI brochure's defining-constants table and its ampere section. The framework's definition of $\varepsilon_0$ by $(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ is a definition consistent with that exact relation; the uncertainty carried by $\varepsilon_0$ is recorded rather than hidden. The dimensional checks of the framework's equations and couplings are developed on the companion examples page of this pair. No numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted and no experiment is claimed.

before.title: Charge parameter, frame charge and current densities, volume charge and flux, and the four-current
before.statement: Let the laboratory region and its chart be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Charge parameter] The framework takes a real charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$, measured in coulombs, attached to a source; its sign is the sign of the source and it is a parameter of the model. Charge quantisation is not asserted. (b) [Smooth source fields] A smooth (volume) source field on $\Omega\times I$ is a pair $(\rho,J)$ of maps $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is continuous on $\Omega\times I$ and of class $C^1$ wherever a displayed equation differentiates it; $\rho$ is the frame charge density (C m$^{-3}$) and $J$ the frame current density (A m$^{-2}$). For each $t\in I$: the charge of a compact Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$ at time $t$ is $Q(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)\,dy$, the Riemann integral over a Jordan set ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]); and for each oriented surface patch in $\Omega$ with unit normal field $n_S$ the current flux at time $t$ is $\int_S J(y,t)\cdot n_S(y)\,dS$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). Point sources and sheet sources are not source fields in this sense; they are different objects, defined by their own pairings when the framework uses them. (c) [Covariant identification] Write $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The framework adopts as a model premise the identification of the charge-current of a source with a vector field of the affine Minkowski model, and hence the component transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$ between inertial charts. This is a model premise, not a theorem about physical currents. (d) [Density versus scalar multiplier] Suppose in addition that the identified $j$ is $C^1$ and equals $\rho_0U$ for a $C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $C^1$ scalar field $\rho_0$, the scalar multiplier. With the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$ (so $u^0=1$ and $u^i=U^i/U^0$), clause (vii) of the supplier gives $j=(\rho_0U^0)u$; comparing the time component with $j^0=c\rho$ gives $\rho=\rho_0U^0/c$. The frame density $\rho$ and the scalar multiplier $\rho_0$ are distinct objects: they agree exactly when $U^0=1$ (equivalently, where the source is at rest in the chart), and $\rho_0$ is the Lorentz rest density of the source model. The direction $u$ is a normalized chart direction, not assumed unit- or four-velocity normalized; when the spatial coordinate velocity interpretation is adopted, it has components $cu^i$. (e) [Scope] This definition fixes the source objects of the smooth branch and their transformation interface. It asserts no conservation law (that is proved for stated source classes) and no regularity of singular sources.
before.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition. The charge $Q(V,t)$ is the integral of a continuous function over a compact Jordan-measurable set, so it is the Riemann integral of [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]; the flux is the surface integral of [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]. Clause (c) is the explicit model premise that licenses the use of the vector transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$; the supplier itself states that the identification of a physical charge-current with a vector field is a model premise, and this item records it as such. Clause (d) is a direct substitution into the supplier's clause (vii): $j=\rho_0U=\rho_0U^0u=j^0u$, so the supplier's coordinate density is $j^0=c\rho$ in this framework's normalisation, and the displayed relation between $\rho$ and $\rho_0$ follows; the supplier's own warning that the coordinate density and the scalar multiplier differ unless $U^0=1$ is retained. No integration or differentiation of the fields is used beyond the cited definitions, and no conservation law is asserted.

after.title: Charge parameter, frame charge and current densities, volume charge and flux, and the four-current
after.statement:
Let the laboratory region and its chart be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Charge parameter] The framework takes a real charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$, measured in coulombs, attached to a source; its sign is the sign of the source and it is a parameter of the model. Charge quantisation is not asserted. (b) [Smooth source fields] A smooth (volume) source field on $\Omega\times I$ is a pair $(\rho,J)$ of maps $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is continuous on $\Omega\times I$ and of class $C^1$ wherever a displayed equation differentiates it; $\rho$ is the frame charge density (C m$^{-3}$) and $J$ the frame current density (A m$^{-2}$). For each fixed $t\in I$ retain the compact Jordan branch: if $V\subseteq\Omega$ is compact and Jordan measurable, define $Q_R(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)dy$ by [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], with integrability supplied by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]. For the full measurable-volume branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the published Lebesgue-measure interface. If $V$ is any bounded Lebesgue-measurable subset with compact closure $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$, define
$$Q(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)d\lambda_3(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}F_t(y)\mathbf1_V(y)d\lambda_3(y),$$
where $F_t=\rho(\cdot,t)$ on $\Omega$ and $0$ elsewhere; the signed integral is defined through its positive and negative parts ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). This integral is absolutely finite, since $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded on $\overline V$ and $V$ has finite Lebesgue measure. On the compact Jordan branch, under the same Countable Choice assumption, $Q=Q_R$ by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]. The empty region has charge zero in both branches. The current flux remains defined independently: for each oriented surface patch in $\Omega$ with unit normal field $n_S$ the current flux at time $t$ is $\int_S J(y,t)\cdot n_S(y)\,dS$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). Point sources and sheet sources are not source fields in this sense; they are different objects, defined by their own pairings when the framework uses them. (c) [Covariant identification] Write $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The framework adopts as a model premise the identification of the charge-current of a source with a vector field of the affine Minkowski model, and hence the component transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$ between inertial charts. This is a model premise, not a theorem about physical currents. (d) [Frame density, scalar multiplier and the normalized material branch] Suppose additionally that the identified $j$ is $C^1$ and $j=\rho_0U$, with a $C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $C^1$ real scalar multiplier $\rho_0$. Since $U^0>0$, define the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$, so $u^0=1$, $u^i=U^i/U^0$. Then $j=(\rho_0U^0)u$ and, because the electromagnetic convention is $j^0=c\rho$,
$$\rho=\rho_0U^0/c,\qquad J^i=\rho_0U^i=c\rho\,u^i.$$
Pointwise equality $\rho=\rho_0$ holds if and only if $\rho_0(U^0-c)=0$, including the zero-multiplier case. Where $\rho_0\ne0$, equality is equivalent to $U^0=c$, which does not alone imply $U^i=0$ for an arbitrary future timelike $U$. Thus a scalar multiplier is not automatically a Lorentz rest charge density. The direction $u$ is chart normalized, with no unit or proper-four-velocity normalization imposed in this general branch; if its coordinate velocity interpretation is adopted, the spatial velocity is $v^i:=cu^i$.
For the separate convective source model, explicitly assume that $U$ is the material proper-time four-velocity, normalized by $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. This is an additional model condition, not a consequence of the factorization $j=\rho_0U$. In that branch, $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $|v|<c$, $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and
$$\rho=\gamma\rho_0,\qquad J=\rho v.$$
Here $\rho_0$ is the rest charge density of this stipulated convective model: in a comoving inertial frame $U=(c,0,0,0)$ and $j=(c\rho_0,0,0,0)$. The equality $\rho=\rho_0$ then holds exactly where $\rho_0=0$ or $v=0$ (equivalently $\gamma=1$). Both signs of charge and the zero-density case are retained. (e) [Scope] This definition fixes the source objects of the smooth branch and their transformation interface. It asserts no conservation law (that is proved for stated source classes) and no regularity of singular sources.
after.strategy:
Keep clauses (a)-(c) as explicit source types and the adopted physical identification. The compact Jordan branch uses [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]] and [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]; flux uses [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]. For the broader Lebesgue branch assume the explicitly stated Countable Choice, without Dependent Choice or a convergence/FTC assumption. Fix $t$ and an admitted nonempty $V$. The continuous function $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded by $M_t<\infty$ in absolute value on compact $\overline V$ by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]. Its zero extension $F_t$ is Borel: for every open $O\subseteq\mathbb R$, the inverse image inside the open set $\Omega$ is relatively open and hence open in $\mathbb R^3$; add the closed complement of $\Omega$ precisely when $0\in O$. This is also the open-set form of [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]. Under Countable Choice, Borel sets are Lebesgue measurable ([[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]) and bounded measurable $V$ has finite measure ([[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]]). Positive/negative parts and their restrictions by $\mathbf1_V$ are measurable by [[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]]. The bound $|F_t|\mathbf1_V\le M_t\mathbf1_V$ and [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]] give
$$\int|F_t|\mathbf1_Vd\lambda_3\le M_t\lambda_3(V)<\infty,$$
where the indicator integral is its simple-function value by [[prop-the-nonnegative-integral-agrees-with-the-simple-integral]]. This proves exactly the absolute signed integrability required by [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]] and defines $Q$ using the nonnegative restrictions of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. For empty $V$ the product is zero. On compact Jordan $V$, the continuous density restricted to V has a bounded Borel zero extension to a bounding rectangle, so the exact compact-Jordan clause of [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], also under Countable Choice, identifies the two finite integral values. The algebraic supplier [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]](vii) gives $j=\rho_0U=\rho_0U^0u$; its coordinate density is $j^0$, whereas the present SI source convention defines $j^0=c\rho$. Division by $c>0$ gives $\rho=\rho_0U^0/c$ and $\rho-\rho_0=\rho_0(U^0-c)/c$, proving exactly the stated equality cases. The spatial components give $J^i=c\rho u^i$. Neither $U^0=c$ nor chart normalization $u^0=1$ is a proper-four-velocity condition.
In the additional normalized material model, write $v=c(U^1,U^2,U^3)/U^0$. The norm equation $-(U^0)^2+|U_{\mathrm{sp}}|^2=-c^2$ gives $(U^0)^2(1-|v|^2/c^2)=c^2$, and future timelikeness gives $U^0>0$ and $|v|<c$, so $U^0=c\gamma$. This is the exact four-velocity/relative-velocity content of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]; substitution gives $\rho=\gamma\rho_0$ and $J=\rho v$. In its comoving frame $U^0=c$, hence the source convention identifies the scalar multiplier with the stipulated rest-frame density. Since $\gamma=1$ if and only if $v=0$, the normalized equality cases follow, including $\rho_0=0$. All density readings remain within the adopted current model; no conservation, measurement, general current factorization, force law or singular-source regularity is deduced.

before.title: A smooth compactly supported density and a point charge on a trajectory are different source classes
before.statement: This example is conditional on the definitions [[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-fields]] and the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], and it uses the Countable Choice assumption AC_omega named below where the published embedding theorem carries it. (a) [Smooth source] Let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ be nonnegative with $\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\,dy=1$ (for instance any nonzero nonnegative smooth compactly supported bump divided by its finite nonzero integral), let $q\in\mathbb R$, and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set containing $\operatorname{supp}f$. Then $\rho:=qf$ and $J:=0$ is a smooth source field of [[def-em-sources]]: $\rho$ is compactly supported and of class $C^\infty$, hence continuous, and for every compact Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$ containing $\operatorname{supp}f$ the charge is $Q(V,t)=q\int f=q$ at every time $t$, so the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] applies to this source. (b) [Point source] Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval and $z:I\to\mathbb R^3$ a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $t\mapsto(z(t),t)$ is proper into $\Omega\times I$ ([[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]; properness is automatic when $\Omega\times I$ is the whole ambient domain or when $I=\mathbb R$). For $q\in\mathbb R$, the pairings $\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_I\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$ and $\langle J,\psi\rangle:=q\int_Iz'(t)\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$, for $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$, are the point-source distributions of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]: they are distributions ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]) satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in the distributional sense. At each fixed time $t$ this model assigns the charge $q\cdot\mathbf 1_{z(t)\in V}$ to a Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$, and its instantaneous spatial density is the evaluation functional $q\delta_{z(t)}$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), $\varphi\mapsto q\,\varphi(z(t))$; a source field of the smooth branch instead gives the integrals $\varphi\mapsto\int_\Omega\rho(y,t)\varphi(y)\,dy$ of its continuous density. (c) [The two classes differ] Fix $t\in I$, put $z_0:=z(t)\in\Omega$ and suppose $q\ne0$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice AC_omega only as it is carried by [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] in the argument below, through the injectivity of the regular-distribution map ([[def-countable-choice]]). Then no locally integrable $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ represents the point charge: there is no such $\rho$ whose regular distribution ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]) satisfies $\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=q\,\varphi(z_0)$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$. Indeed, if $\rho$ did, then on the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$ every test vanishes at $z_0$, so the regular distribution of the restriction of $\rho$ is zero, and injectivity gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere there ([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); since $\{z_0\}$ is Lebesgue-null ([[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]) and a union of two null sets is null ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]), $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. The regular distribution depends only on the almost-everywhere class, so $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=0$ for a cutoff $\varphi_0\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$ ([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]), while the assumed identity gives $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$: a contradiction. Hence the point source is not a source field of the smooth branch of [[def-em-sources]] (whose densities are continuous functions), and the smooth-branch equations are not applied to it pointwise; the point source enters the framework only through its distributional pairings. (d) [Conclusion] The two source classes carry the same parameter $q$ and the same total charge $q$ (the smooth density integrates to $q$; the point model assigns charge $q$ to regions containing the particle), but they are different mathematical objects with different regularity, and they enter the framework through different branches. This example asserts no field value at $z(t)$ and contains no measurement or empirical claim.
before.strategy: Direct computations and one short contradiction. (a) $\rho=qf$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, hence continuous and bounded; for a compact Jordan-measurable $V$ containing the support, the integral of $\rho$ over $V$ equals $q\int f=q$ by the definition of $f$ and additivity of the integral over the support complement ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]). (b) The pairings and the continuity equation are exactly the content of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] under its properness hypothesis; the fixed-time reading $q\delta_{z(t)}$ is the evaluation functional of [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]. (c) Suppose $u_\rho=q\delta_{z_0}$ with $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. On the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\setminus\{z_0\})$ one has $u_\rho(\varphi)=q\varphi(z_0)=0$; the injectivity clause of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], which carries AC_omega, gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$. The singleton $\{z_0\}$ is null by [[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]], and the union of the exceptional null set with $\{z_0\}$ is null by finite subadditivity ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]), so $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. By the definition of the regular distribution (which depends only on the almost-everywhere class) $u_\rho=0$, i.e. $u_\rho(\varphi)=0$ for every test. The cutoff lemma supplies $\varphi_0$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$, and the assumed identity gives $u_\rho(\varphi_0)=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$, a contradiction. (d) is the bookkeeping of the two total charges. No field equation is solved, no regularity of the point source is asserted beyond its distributional definition, and the only choice principle used is the Countable Choice carried explicitly by the embedding theorem's injectivity.

before.title: The electromagnetic two-form, its observer decomposition and the four-current
before.statement:

unchanged_coupling_review.statement:
Adopt as physical postulates of this framework, on the spacetime and particle model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] and on the special-relativity particle model [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]: (i) [Test charge in a prescribed external field] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter ([[def-em-sources]]), $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass, $x:J\to A$ a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline with four-velocity $U$, and let $F$ be a prescribed field of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle. Adopt the equation of motion

$$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),$$

where $\Phi$ is the raised-index operator of the field at the event $x(\tau)$, defined by $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]); equivalently $m\,dU^\mu/d\tau=q\,F^{\mu\nu}U_\nu$. The particle's own field is excluded from $F$: this is the external-field coupling, and it defines no self-force. (ii) [Continuum matter coupling] For a smooth source $(\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] interacting with the field through an explicitly stated matter model to which this coupling applies, adopt the force density $\rho E+J\times B$ (unit N m$^{-3}$) and the power density $J\cdot E$ (unit W m$^{-3}$) as the electromagnetic source terms of that matter model; they describe the local interaction of the field with matter and are not a property of a prescribed current alone. (iii) [Scope] The rest mass and the charge are inputs; $m$ is not derived within electromagnetism. The coupling is adopted for constant $q$ and $m>0$; no magnetic-monopole coupling, no radiation reaction and no self-force are included. In particular the nonrelativistic coordinate statement $mr''=q(E+r'\times B)$ is not adopted as exact: the adopted statement is the covariant one of clause (i), and any low-speed statement requires its own approximation hypotheses and error bounds.
unchanged_coupling_review.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. The exposition must state the exact data (constant charge, externally supplied positive rest mass, future timelike C^2 worldline, prescribed external field C^1 near the graph), name the raised-index operator $\Phi$ with its defining identity and index form from [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] so that the equation is unambiguous, and state the exclusion of the particle's own field. Clause (ii) is a formulation premise for matter models, with its units fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]] and its cross product the spatial one of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; it is not a derivation from the field equations. Clause (iii) records the scope: no self-force, no radiation reaction, no magnetic monopole, and no exact Newtonian law. Empirical support for the coupling is a nonlogical relation of the framework; the item claims no verification and no measured value.
